analysis: The supplied units (docs/reference/configuration.md head lines 675-1212) are documentation only. The changed ranges per file_changes are line 3 (date bump) and line 201 (the `backend.enabled_models` row). That row sits outside the supplied text units, so I could only see it in the patch excerpt, which is truncated. No executable code changed in the examined scope. The line 201 change documents an operator filter on model loading: a nonempty `enabled_models`, plus the models the daemon started with, blocks coordinator `load_model`, `prefetch_model` and `desired_models` for models outside the list unless Autopilot is on. This narrows coordinator-driven model loading (A-004/A-018 context) and is not a regression in the docs. The Swift enforcement (`ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift` `operatorFilterAllows`) is not supplied, so I cannot confirm the code matches the description, including the Autopilot exception and alias-successor behavior. The supplied units cover the cache and cluster configuration text. They are unchanged, and I reviewed them for contradictions with T-041. The cache storage docs (`cache.directory`, `cache.volume_uuid`, the `DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE` DEBUG-only behavior, the TTL max of 1800 s, the persistent write budget) match the T-041 posture. The cluster approval, fetch and registration docs describe strict validation and existing trust contracts, with no new attack surface stated. No findings. A deeper check of the actual enabled_models enforcement code in a source pass would be useful, but nothing here establishes a vulnerability.
